summary: The new retention rule conflicts with the benchmark’s security contract, archives an incomplete benchmark state, and lacks a safe append protocol for the shared ledger branch.

findings.title: Raw benchmark logs are pushed despite the security boundary
findings.trigger: A reviewer stdout/stderr log contains a token, proprietary source excerpt, or another sensitive model-output fragment, and the delivery follows the new archive instruction.
findings.consequence: The sensitive content is committed and pushed to `llm-ledger`, where it is exposed to repository readers and retained in Git history.
findings.evidence: The new rule requires committing and pushing `.review-benchmark/runs/` at workflow.md:19-23. Those runs include prompts and per-reviewer stdout/stderr logs at tools/llm-review-bench/README.md:229-245, while design/llm-review-benchmark.md:317-319 explicitly states that raw logs may contain sensitive fragments and must not be committed.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not push raw runs to the repository without an approved security boundary. Use an access-controlled archive or a documented redaction/allowlist step, and reconcile the authoritative benchmark security contract before enabling retention.

findings.title: The archive omits the benchmark's paired gold records
findings.trigger: Any normal `llm-review-bench` review is archived using only the two listed directories and the delivery worktree is then removed.
findings.consequence: The archived evaluation can no longer be fully rendered or recomputed: its referenced gold version is absent, so historical labels, recall attribution, and later report generation are lost or fail.
findings.evidence: workflow.md:19-21 names only `.review-benchmark/runs/` and `.agents/reviews/`. Every benchmark run finalizes with `createGold: true` at tools/llm-review-bench/src/commands/run.ts:45-48, but gold is stored in the sibling `.review-benchmark/gold/<run-id>/` tree, outside run directories, at tools/llm-review-bench/README.md:223-257 and design/llm-review-benchmark.md:164-171. Report rendering reloads the evaluation's referenced gold version at tools/llm-review-bench/src/evaluation/pipeline.ts:243-250.
findings.suggestedFix: Define a self-contained, per-run archive layout that retains each run's matching gold records outside reviewer snapshots, plus any required replay metadata, and verify `report` and `rescore` from a fresh archive checkout.

findings.title: Concurrent deliveries have no safe ledger append protocol
findings.trigger: Two owned delivery worktrees finish from the same `llm-ledger` tip, or both observe that the branch does not yet exist, and each tries to archive evidence.
findings.consequence: One push is rejected as non-fast-forward, or concurrent orphan-root initialization creates incompatible histories. The second delivery cannot push its required audit evidence and either blocks cleanup or loses the trail if cleanup proceeds.
findings.evidence: Checkout Isolation is specifically entered when another agent's work is present at workflow.md:8-9, but workflow.md:18-23 directs every such delivery to append to one `llm-ledger` branch without fetch, serialization, merge, or retry instructions. The only documented rejection/rebase loop is for the development-line push at workflow.md:74-76, not this new shared archival branch.
findings.suggestedFix: Specify an append protocol: fetch the remote ledger before staging, initialize its orphan root exactly once, use a dedicated ledger worktree, and retry non-fast-forward updates after integrating the current remote ledger tip. Verify that the pushed tip contains the topic before removing the delivery worktree.
